missionPremise: OPS-21's root-cause finding: setbacks have had no write path to a value since the anti-zombie change (computeTier1Envelope's two branches both decline; write-setback-city.mjs's --apply is held). The chosen path (ADR-031-consistent, same expedient already blessed for CAD rails): write parcel_record_cell cells DIRECTLY from the existing, live, correct ruled-table computation -- never lift the held atom writer, never build a second resolver. This lane (S1) is that writer for the four setback scalars + the setbackRules companion, in-city only, in the five counties P-145 does not yet gate.
completionPredicate: scripts/plan-progress.mjs --sql's S1 row: count(*) of parcel_record_cell rows on the 5 setback rail keys, joined to in-city landing_parcel_jurisdiction rows, WHERE cell_state='unaccounted', across the SIX CTX counties. Measured live at close: 291,055 (six-county scope, includes Hays 48209 which stays 100% unaccounted by design -- P-145 has not landed). Scoped to this lane's own five in-scope counties (48021/48055/48309/48453/48491): 16,880, down from a 2,781,405 baseline (556,281 in-city parcels x 5 rails, ALL unaccounted before this lane ran -- confirmed live, zero pre-existing value/refused/absent-verified rows on any of the 5 rails anywhere in the in-city population). That is a 99.39% reduction, reproducible by a stranger re-running the same predicate query. The residual 16,880 (=3,376 parcels x 5 rails, arithmetically exact -- every deferred parcel's 5 rails move as one unit) is NOT a defect in this lane's writer: every one of those 3,376 parcels has a zoningDistrict cell that is not yet `value` or `refused` (still `unaccounted` or a pre-existing cross-system `not-applicable` drift, see openFinding below) -- a DIFFERENT rail, owned by a DIFFERENT already-existing job (parcel-r5-zoning.mjs), which this dispatch never named as a dependency. Re-running `factory parcel-setback-cells --apply` after zoningDistrict advances further will continue closing this gap with ZERO additional code changes -- the writer itself asks nothing more of the world.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: When a dispatch names a specific cross-repo package as 'the live resolver,' verify the actual call chain (grep the real route's imports), not just that the named package exists and has the right function name. Two packages had the identical exported function signature-ish shape (2-arg vs 3-arg) in two different repos; only one was actually wired to anything live.

A dispatch's enumerated data list (here, '7 ruled-table cities') should be treated as a hypothesis to verify mechanically (probe the real data source per real city_name), never copied as the authoritative scope -- the true population was 3.4x larger. This is the same 'do not hand-author a rail list' discipline rail-keys.js already enforces one layer up, applied to a city dimension nobody had named as needing the same discipline.

A published 'merge the two divergent copies' package (here, @empressaio/setback-corpus) can be published and correct while BOTH of the repos it was built to unify still read their own stale local copies. Check actual import sites in both consumers before assuming a publish event changed anything live.

A job whose only input from another store is a READ (not the job's own eventual write) still needs that store's connection opened on a dry run, or the dry-run preview crashes / silently no-ops. Caught by live verification against real data before deploy, not by unit tests with fake clients (which happily accept a null connection you never actually call).

Strongest proof (peer-supplied, re-verified at source via `gh run list --workflow=ldt-pin-staleness`): the SAME factory commit 63a606b1 passed on push (16:12:02Z) and failed on the scheduled trigger (20:30:05Z) once LDT main moved underneath it at 20:02:15Z -- rules out any factory commit as cause by construction. The gate went red twice in one day, not once: a 15:57:23Z scheduled run also failed (on 83c98f97, before #131 re-greened it). Six _LDT_SHA bumps landed in ~38 hours (#113 through #131); CTX-PIN4 is the seventh. The cron is configured `0 */6 * * *` but GitHub delivered it 2.5-5h late in the observed runs (10:48:32Z/15:57:23Z/20:30:05Z against nominal 06:00/12:00/18:00Z) -- so real worst-case drift-detection latency is closer to 11 hours than 6; do not reason about the detection window from the cron string alone. Flagged to doc-repo-4a, who compiled CTX-PIN4 (P-124) to fix it; not fixed by this lane.

Get a workflow-vs-job name pair exactly right before writing it into a durable artifact: this close originally inverted it ("the check workflow, job check-ldt-pin-staleness") when it's really the ldt-pin-staleness WORKFLOW whose job id is check -- caught by a peer review, the mistake would have cost the next reader a `gh run list --workflow=check` failing with 'could not find any workflows named check'. When citing a CI job by name, read the workflow YAML's own `name:` and job-id fields directly rather than reconstructing the pair from a check-run listing.

When two mechanisms could each explain a live discrepancy (a workflow's push-vs-schedule triggers, here), the strongest falsifier is the SAME input observed under both, at two times, with the intervening external change identified -- not just 'the state was already this way one generation back'. A peer's re-framing of an already-correct finding into its cleanest form is still worth adopting.

A control's absence (here, no pull_request trigger on ldt-pin-staleness) is itself a claim to verify before proposing to add it back -- read the file's own header comment first. A peer's mission (CTX-PIN4) briefly carried an item to 'fix' this exact gap before its own author caught, from a detail in this close, that the YAML already explains the exclusion at length as a deliberate DEV_PROCESS 2.0 tradeoff (a permanently-red gate is a dead gate). Nearly shipped a fix for something that was never broken.

Do not assume 'the mission's dispatch premise about a package name' is settled just because the package exists and exports a same-named function -- @hauska-engine/adapters exports getSetbackTableForZoning too, with a different (3-arg) signature, and is not what anything live calls.
